main_body: A bonsai-style pine tree: a diagonal brown trunk with three flat-topped green foliage pads (a large upper canopy, a right pad and a left pad).
top_band: none as a distinct surface; the canopy is an organic leaf mass shaded in greens (L 88-110 highlights over 46-69 darker greens), with no separate horizontal top band and front face
evidence: The object is organic: foliage pads and a slanted trunk, with no horizontal surface contract to break. The column scan at x=22 shows a mixed green run from rows 1-13, a gap, then the trunk from rows 17-44. Pads have lighter upper-left tops and darker undersides, which reads as volume. It is not a rigid structure (cabinet, seat, container), so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply strictly. There is no side face and no flat elevation panel. Passes as an organic plant.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 8 colours per tile, against 427-567 colours and about 108 per tile for the references. The foliage uses about 4 greens (L 46, 69, 88, 110) with a checker-like dithering and no per-leaf clumps with highlights. The trunk has 3 browns plus a dark outline. 37% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, and the near-black #0f1e16 outline around the canopy and #231d28 around the trunk form a fairly uniform sticker-like line. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so the dither adds some texture. Overall it is much thinner and flatter than the Beodeul trees in shading depth and information density.
